data.label: SecureTool (guard ON)
data.name: customTool
data.description: A Custom Tool protected by the Zero-Context Guard. $vars is absent; the secret is accessed only via $secureRequest.

inputs.name: secure_echo
inputs.description: Call the public httpbin echo endpoint using a protected fake API key. The guard injects the Authorization header; the sandbox never sees the key value.
inputs.schema: z.object({ message: z.string().describe('A short message to echo') })

data.label: UnsecuredTool (guard OFF)
data.name: customTool
data.description: A Custom Tool WITHOUT secret bindings. It attempts to read $vars to illustrate what an unguarded tool can access.

inputs.name: unsafe_vars_dump
inputs.description: Attempt to dump the $vars object. On a guarded tool this would not be possible because $vars would be absent.

data.label: Tool Agent
data.name: toolAgent
data.description: Demo agent — call the SecureTool to show the guard working, or the UnsecuredTool to show the contrast.

inputs.systemMessage:
You are a demo assistant for the Zero-Context Guard hackathon project.

You have two tools:
1. secure_echo — protected by the Zero-Context Guard. The sandbox never sees the API key.
2. unsafe_vars_dump — legacy tool with no bindings. It can see $vars keys (all fake here).

When the user asks to 'show the guard', call secure_echo.
When the user asks to 'show the contrast' or 'show unguarded', call unsafe_vars_dump.
Explain what happened in plain language.

chatflow.name: Zero-Context Guard Demo
chatflow.description: IBM Bob Hackathon — Theme 2. Demonstrates the Zero-Context Guard contrast: one guarded tool (secret injected server-side, $vars absent) versus one unguarded tool ($vars present). All credential values are fake.

_meta.note: FAKE credentials only. The credentialId 'PLACEHOLDER_CREDENTIAL_ID' must be replaced after import. See deploy/README.md.
